sentences.text:
Author: B. Vijaysen Reddy
Bench: B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Writ Petition No.11018 Of 2023
Order :

(ORAL) The writ petition is filed seeking to declare action of respondent Nos.3 and 4 in calling the petitioners to the Police Station frequently without there being any complaint, as illegal and arbitrary.
2. Heard Sri M.Ajay Kumar, learned counsel for petitioners and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home and perused the material available on record.
3.

In the written instructions dated 20.04.2023 received by the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, it is stated that respondent No.5 lodged a complaint against the petitioners in Crime No.67 of 2023 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2) (n), 354(c) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860(for short the 'IPC').
4.

Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home submitted that as offences registered in F.I.R.
No.67 of 2023 is under Sections 376(2) (n), 354(c) and 506 of the I.P.C., petitioners cannot claim protection under Section 41-A of the Cr.P.C.
A copy of the F.I.R. along with written instructions dated 20.04.2023 is served on the learned counsel for the petitioners.
4. Recording the same, the writ petition is disposed of.
However, petitioners are given liberty to seek appropriate relief in connection with F.I.R. No.67 of 2023.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.

__ B. VIJAYSEN REDDY, J 20.04.2023 Lpd THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE B. VIJAYSEN REDDY WRIT PETITION No.11018 OF 2023 April 20, 2023 LPD Motam Rakesh vs The State Of Telangana on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120842522/
